text:
lin: heads up, after yesterday's kernel swap i see weird PP bubble growth on the 1F1B runs
anya: u + logs?
lin: pasted perfdump from a 4-GPU run (microbatch=4):
```
step 1: forward gpu0 12ms
step 2: forward gpu1 14ms
step 3: all-reduce 9ms
step 4: backward gpu1 20ms
step 5: all-reduce 11ms
step 6: backward gpu0 22ms
idle gaps: 8-15ms between fwd/bwd
end-to-end step latency: 118ms
```
devon: that all-reduce is kinda high, did the kernel fallback to nccl ring?
mike: we shipped the new fused-allreduce kernel last week to some clusters only, others fallback to pointwise plus NCCL. might explain variance
sanction: perfbot: regression detected: +12% tail latency on pp-1f1b workload since commit d4f9e3
anya: lin, can you repro with microbatch=8? bubble behaviour often improves with larger microbatches
lin: ran microbatch=8, same model, same infra: overall latency 104ms, idle gaps shrank to 3-6ms
lin: but token throughput dropped a bit and KV cache thrash increased for certain prompt patterns
sasha: KV cache thrash? details?
lin: when we increased microbatch, cache hits dropped 7% for prefix-heavy traces — looks like sequence packing changed alignments, causing cache key eviction pattern to change
devon: hmm kernel selection + microbatching + seq packing interplay. we need a test matrix: kernel variant x microbatch x seq-dist
mike: i'll spin a canary with fused-allreduce enabled for this pool and run the matrix overnight
infra-bot: deploy started: canary/fused-allreduce -> 4 instances (gpu-pool-3)
lin: also ran profiler flamegraph, attaching snippet:
```
flame: 40% fwd kernels (matmul), 30% comm (all-reduce), 20% kv-lookup, 10% misc
note: comm stack shows multiple small collectives, not aggregated\```
anya: small collectives are the killer for 1F1B. if we can batch reductions across microbatches we reduce per-step comm overhead
sasha: suggestion: try microbatch accumulation with delayed all-reduce (accumulate grads across microbatches before reduce) for eval-only to see effect
devon: careful: delayed all-reduce changes semantics for optimizer during training, but for inference we can safely aggregate activations and do a single reduce per group
mike: confirmed: canary fused-allreduce + microbatch=4 => all-reduce median down from 9ms -> 3ms, total step latency 92ms
lin: nice. but we still see a small regression vs pre-kernel-swap baseline (about +4% tail)
anya: could be kernel compile path changed matrix tiling leading to worse small-seq perf
lin: i dumped kernel choice log: new kernel picks matmul-tiling-16x64 for layer 3-9, old used 8x128 on same hw
sasha: tiling tradeoffs differ by seq length; could explain sequence-dependent perf changes
devon: action items: 1) run full matrix overnight (kernel variant, microbatch 2/4/8, seq-dist A/B/C) 2) enable fused-allreduce canary on staging 3) add KV hit telemetry by seq alignment 4) add an aggregated-reduce experiment to schedule (debug-only)
lin: agreed. i'll add a lightweight experiment harness into perfbench that varies seq packing to reproduce cache effect
mike: i'll push canary and collect results; tagging @anya @devon for run ownership
perfbot: job scheduled: perf-matrix-1765432100 -> expected end in 10h
lin: thanks. if we reduce small collectives and adjust kernel tiling for short sequences we should recover bubble efficiency
anya: and we should add a microbatch-sensitive kernel selector heuristic: prefer tilings that minimize inter-step variance for seq<64
lin: yup. i'll prototype heuristic and open a PR after results. :thumbsup:
